title: Show an instant to a viewer

blocks.text: An `Instant` is a point on the UTC timeline with no calendar and no clock, so a formatter cannot print it until it knows whose clock to read.

Write `ViewerStamp.format(Instant instant, ZoneId viewer)`. It shows the instant the way a viewer in `viewer` sees it on their **own clock**, in **English whatever the server's default locale**, like `Fri, Mar 15, 2024 11:30 PM EDT`: the short weekday, the short month, the day, the year, the time on the **12-hour clock** with `AM` or `PM`, and the zone's short name.

cases.says: An afternoon instant shows its weekday, date, 12-hour time, AM or PM and the zone's short name.
03:30 UTC on March 16 is still Friday, March 15 at 11:30 PM for a viewer in New York.
A quarter past midnight shows as 12:15 AM, and five past noon as 12:05 PM.
On a server whose default locale is German, the weekday, month and AM or PM are still English.

concepts: An Instant has no calendar fields, so a formatter prints it only after withZone, or after converting it to a ZonedDateTime.
h is the 12-hour clock from 1 to 12 and needs a for AM or PM, while H runs from 0 to 23.
